security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates ACE memory instructions (ace.prov, ace.export, ace.import) as single atomic TCG memory operations, enforcing internal ordering or fixed granularity within the instruction, when the spec now requires decomposition into unordered component memory operations of arbitrary granularity with no atomicity guarantees. Additionally, QEMU multi-hart SMP emulation fails to enforce RVWMO (or RVTSO if Ztso is implemented) at the ACE instruction level while simultaneously permitting any intra-instruction reordering of component memory ops.
security_spec.summary: ACE memory instructions lost their 'appears as sequence of individual reads/stores/loads' guarantees and gained explicit non-atomicity with unordered intra-instruction decomposition of arbitrary granularity; QEMU TCG must not emit ACE memory ops as single atomic transactions and must correctly model RVWMO/RVTSO at instruction level while permitting arbitrary intra-instruction reordering across SMP harts.

findings.finding: ACE (ace.prov, ace.export, ace.import) memory model instructions are not implemented in this QEMU codebase. No decode entries, helper functions, TCG translation code, CSR definitions, or any reference to ACE exists in target/riscv/. The only 'ACE' hits in the entire repo are for unrelated x86 AMD crypto (target/i386/cpu.h:1243) and USB quirk entries.
